messages:
Leah (AE): Heads up 60; Zenith follow-up: they want a firm commit for production POC. Target sustained ~1.2k rps, typical payloads 33 tokens, occasional doc loads up to 45k tokens. They also expect 2.5x burst for 102 secs during promos.
Ravi (Solutions): Quick read: we should split traffic by profile: short chat pool vs longcontext pool. Reserved capacity sized for sustained baseline; burst credits for promo windows.
Kai (SRE): Agree. Need to decide reserved_gpu count. Ballpark: with our current kernel perf, 1 GPU handles ~150 short-rps (3k tokens) at p95 <150ms. That implies ~8 GPUs baseline for short traffic. Long sessions require separate instances because KV/cache and memory differ.
Noor (Sales Eng): Zenith says long-docs are rare (~3%) but high latency tolerance (p95 <6s). Short calls are 97% and must be <150ms p95.
Ravi (Solutions): Proposal: reserve 8 gpus for short pool, 2 gpus for longcontext pool, reserve burst escrow to allow up to +12 gpus transiently. Add quantized fallback for bursts.
Kai (SRE): Draft autoscale policy snippet (for SOW):
```
min_gpus: 6
reserved_gpus: 10
max_burst_gpus: 22
burst_window_seconds: 600
burst_credits: 1800
kv_preheat_minutes: 15
cooldown_seconds: 300
routing:
  short_pool: reserved_gpus: 8
  long_pool: reserved_gpus: 2
  fallback_model: quantized-lite
```
Ravi (Solutions): Notes: burst_credits expressed in GPU-seconds; we'll translate to dollars in the cost table. Also recommend policy to cap per-customer burst spend.
Leah (AE): Can you map burst_credits to a 1h, 3h promo cost scenario? They asked for worst-case estimate.
Ravi (Solutions): Will run numbers and push a short table.
Noor (Sales Eng): Security question: during burst instances, do audit logs and KMS usage remain customer-isolated? Zenith flagged this in questionnaire.
Kai (SRE): Yes. All instances, including burst, authenticate with the customer's KMS (or our managed KMS if they opt). Audit logs are centralized to their audit sink and write identical entries. For Private deployment we can ensure no egress.
Leah (AE): Contract question: do we need an addendum for burst escrow billing vs reserved?
Ravi (Solutions): For Dedicated we can incorporate as part of the commit. For Hosted we add a one-page billing addendum specifying escrow rates, burn rules, and out-of-escrow behavior (graceful throttling). I'll draft.
Noor (Sales Eng): Also propose "eco-burst" tier: cheaper quantized model for bursts, auto-switch if burst spend exceeds X. Zenith might like cost control.
Kai (SRE): Canary idea: if they deploy new model near promo use canary with rollback thresholds. Add to SOW.
Leah (AE): Action items:
- Ravi: cost table for baseline and 1h/3h promo (deliver by EOD PT)
- Kai: run a 3x burst sim and validate kv_preheat_minutes=15 suffices (tomorrow)
- Noor: draft SOW bullets (eco-burst and canary rollback) and security note for KMS/audit (tomorrow)
- Leah: confirm promo schedule with Zenith and capture expected traffic shapes
OpsBot: Runbook created: /runs/4981-burst-escrow-preheat-checklist (includes escalation, preheat job template, rollback steps).
Ravi (Solutions): FYI: if their long docs are more common than reported, we should re-evaluate reserved sizing; ask for histogram of sequence lengths.
Leah (AE): I'll get telemetry samples and pass them along.
Kai (SRE): Plan to preheat KV 20 minutes before promo and run a short warmup load. Add 5-10 minute preheat cron before the window.
Noor (Sales Eng): I'll add an optional training workshop to help Zenith instrument their client telemetry for us.
Leah (AE): Thanks team. Once Ravi posts the cost table I'll include it in the SOW and share with Zenith. :white_check_mark:
